results.title: Bridging corporate purpose and strategic renewal
results.content: # Bridging corporate purpose and strategic renewal: A review and future research agenda. There is growing interest in the strategic role of corporate purpose in processes of strategic renewal, but existing research appears fragmented and offers mixed insights. To address this issue, this study develops a systematic literature review to identify the links between corporate purpose and strategic renewal across diverse research streams. The proposed research agenda is organized around three main objectives: *testing and elaborating, contextualizing,* and *theorizing* the relationship between corporate purpose and strategic renewal. Her research focuses on understanding the relationship between corporate purpose and strategic renewal across levels of analysis, adopting mainly qualitative methods. His research appeared in journals such as Journal of Management Studies, Strategy Science, and Family Business Review. **Josip Kotlar** (email: ) is Full Professor of Strategy, Innovation, and Family Business at the School of Management of Politecnico di Milano (Italy).

results.title: Contextualizing corporate entrepreneurship: a systematic ...
results.content: The contexts considered in our review are business, spatial, social, and institutional, derived from Welter (Citation2011), and organizational and ownership aspects, derived from Zahra (Citation2015) and Foss et al. The need to understand the different contextual variables influencing the entrepreneurial efforts of a firm calls for further research to advance the knowledge and theoretical perspectives of the area (Zahra Citation2015), especially considering that entrepreneurs are embedded in different contexts simultaneously (Korsgaard et al. Bibliometric studies have clustered the structure and theoretical foundations of the entrepreneurial organization literature (Lampe, Kraft, and Bausch Citation2020) and mapped the evolution of CE as a research field (Urbano et al. Nonetheless, the domain of CE has not systematically considered the quest to contextualize entrepreneurship research (e.g. Welter Citation2011). “Corporate Entrepreneurship: A Systematic Literature Review and Future Research Agenda.” *Small Business Economics* 59 (4): 1–25. “International Venturing by Emerging Economy Firms: The Effects of Firm Capabilities, Home Country Networks, and Corporate Entrepreneurship.” *Journal of International Business Studies* 38 (4): 519–540.
